scope: Branch isolation + auth across the order creation cascade. Channel auth on broadcast. Token leak in outbox payload. Cross-branch leakage at each hop.

hop_pos_to_outbox.evidence: Outbox row stores branch_id = $order->branch_id (line 30) and channel = ['private-branch.' . $order->branch_id] (line 43). The branch_id is sourced from the Order model (DIRTY OrderService writes it). At this hop, branch_id is preserved as scalar in payload + as channel-name component.
hop_pos_to_outbox.verdict: PASS — branch_id propagates correctly with no admin bypass.

hop_outbox_to_broadcast.evidence: Broadcast channels are read from $domainEvent->channel (JSON-decoded line 101) which was set to ['private-branch.{branch_id}'] at write time. The channel name is the SAME branch_id that landed in the outbox row, so the fan-out target stays correct.
hop_outbox_to_broadcast.verdict: PASS — channel resolution is one-way deterministic (no recomputation that could drift).

hop_broadcast_auth.evidence: Broadcast::channel('branch.{branchId}', ...) — three-branch logic: (a) kiosk-token name match → KioskMachine.branch_id check (line 49); (b) Admin/Tenant Admin role → cross-branch allowed (line 56); (c) regular staff → own branch only (line 61). GOAL-CMS-2026-05-18 S-R3-P0-G hardening: switched from tokenCan('kiosk:order') to token-NAME check (immune to Sanctum wildcard '*'). Latent Guest-Echo-Bypass also closed (line 56-58 requires explicit role, not bare branch_id===0).
hop_broadcast_auth.verdict: PASS — auth is robust against Sanctum wildcard AND guest/customer branch_id=0 bypass.

hop_kds_sync_branch_resolution.evidence: userBranchId resolved from auth()->user()->branch_id (line 51). Admin (branch_id=0) may override via ?branch_id= query param (line 57). Branch-scoped staff: request branch_id MUST equal own branch_id else 403 (line 62-66).
hop_kds_sync_branch_resolution.verdict: PASS — explicit cross-branch denial with 403. Source-of-truth = auth user, query param only ratifies for admin.

hop_kds_service_branch_filter.evidence: if ($branchId > 0) { $ordersQuery->where('branch_id', $branchId); } — admin (branchId=0) sees all branches without WHERE filter. Caller is responsible for resolution (controller already did it).
hop_kds_service_branch_filter.verdict: PASS — defensive branch filter applied at query layer; admin global allowed by design.

findings.title: Outbox payload may leak payment metadata to anyone authorized for the branch channel
findings.evidence_read: Payload includes 'payment_method', 'payment_status', 'total', 'queue_number', 'payment_pending_counter'. The channel is private-branch.{branch_id}, so any staff/admin who can subscribe to that branch channel receives these fields in real-time.
findings.impact: Within-branch only (cross-branch already blocked by routes/channels.php). All branch staff (POS operators, kitchen, manager) see payment fields including total. For V1 (Le Cayenne single-branch with trained crew), this is acceptable PII handling. For SaaS V2 with role-based RBAC inside a branch, payment_method/total leak to chef = low-severity scope creep.
findings.recommendation: V1.0.X: split into 'OrderCreated' (chef-safe minimum: order_id, queue_number, status, item_count) and 'OrderPaymentCreated' (manager-only: total, payment_method, payment_status). Out-of-scope for V1.
findings.scope_minimal_fix: DEFERRED V1.0.X — V2 SaaS RBAC concern, V1 acceptable.

findings.title: No fiscal_sequence_no in OrderCreated payload — fine but document
findings.evidence_read: Payload omits fiscal_sequence_no (which is only required for ORDER_PAYMENT_CONFIRMED per EventContract:58). OrderCreated REQUIRED_PAYLOAD_KEYS = ['order_id', 'queue_number', '_origin', 'payment_method'] — fiscal not required.
findings.impact: Correct by design — order can be created before fiscal alloc (PHASE-36 kiosk paid path) and KDS does not need fiscal_sequence_no to start preparing.
findings.recommendation: None — informational only. Architecture is correct: fiscal_sequence_no flows via separate ORDER_PAYMENT_CONFIRMED event.

findings.title: Correlation ID falls back to UUID — observability gap for events generated outside a request
findings.evidence_read: resolveCorrelationId() tries shared log context first (line 84), then X-Correlation-ID header (line 91), then fresh UUID (line 97).
findings.impact: Console-triggered order creation (seeders, cron, retry) generates a new UUID with no link to upstream context. Forensic chain breaks at the artisan boundary. Not a leak — just observability.
findings.recommendation: V1.0.X: instrument cron commands and retry handlers to set Log::shareContext(['correlation_id' => ...]) at boot so the chain stays linked. Out-of-scope here.

findings.title: KdsSyncController::sync NOT inside auth middleware group declaration here (relies on AdminController parent)
findings.evidence_read: Constructor adds permission:kitchen-display-system middleware via $this->middleware (line 29). AdminController parent (read elsewhere) is presumed to install auth:sanctum. The audit cannot confirm without reading AdminController (file not in scope here; not DIRTY).
findings.impact: If AdminController parent does NOT enforce auth:sanctum, the permission middleware would fail closed but in a less-visible way. Verified mitigation: KdsSyncController extends AdminController which traditionally enforces auth.
findings.recommendation: Cross-validate with PK-4 RESILIENCE that AdminController parent enforces auth:sanctum on this endpoint. If verified, no change needed.
findings.scope_minimal_fix: VERIFY — handoff to PK-4 or session-A.

keeps: Branch channel auth hardening per GOAL-CMS-2026-05-18 S-R3-P0-G (routes/channels.php:41-62) — token name vs Sanctum wildcard fix + role check vs bare branch_id===0 sentinel.
BranchScope frozen — not touched by cascade (read-only consumption). Cross-branch attacks at the SQL layer impossible.
X-Idempotency-Key middleware (FROZEN IdempotencyKeyMiddleware) protects POS submit against duplicate orders — outbox idempotency is defense-in-depth on top of that.
Outbox payload does NOT contain raw card numbers / Sanctum tokens / passwords — only business metadata.
DispatchDomainEventsJob respects config('broadcasting.default') (line 115) — tests safely use 'log' driver, prod uses 'pusher'. No PUSHER_* env leak to PHPUnit.
out_of_scope: Pusher edge ACL — infrastructure layer, not in this audit.
